case_title: Rohini Sudarshan Gangurde v. The State of Maharashtra & Anr.
accused_victim_relationship: Spouse (marital dispute between the accused and the victim)
statutory_provisions: IPC s.306 (abetment of suicide) read with s.107
evidence_type: Oral statements of complainant and two colleagues; post-mortem report; no suicide note found
trial_court_outcome: Rejected discharge application; charge under s.306 IPC to continue (no verdict or sentence; trial pending)
high_court_outcome: Criminal revision dismissed, upholding the trial court's rejection of discharge
neutral_facts: On 17 February 2020, the victim was found hanging from a balcony of the shared residence where the victim lived with the accused, and neighbours alerted the police. No suicide note was recovered. The post-mortem report recorded no injuries on the body and noted the cause of death as hanging. The same day, the victim's mother lodged a First Information Report alleging that the accused had subjected the victim to physical and mental harassment and beatings over demands for money and for transfer of the dwelling house into the accused's name. The complaint further alleged that the accused insisted the victim not visit the victim's parents or give them money, and sent vulgar messages to the victim's mobile phone. A statement by a colleague of the victim described an incident on 17 October 2019 in which the accused came to the victim's office, rushed towards the victim and was abusive. Another colleague corroborated this incident. According to the accused's version, the victim was addicted to liquor, which caused quarrels between the couple, and the victim may have died out of frustration. The charge-sheet alleged that the accused harassed the victim over money and the house transfer between 7.00 and 7.30 am on the day of death, inducing an attempt at suicide.
offence_severity: Imprisonment up to ten years and fine (no minimum stated)
physical_harm: Death by hanging; no injuries on the body noted in post-mortem
motive: Not identified. alleged: harassment and beating over demands for money and transfer of the dwelling house into the accused's name; the court found no proximate link between the marital dispute and the suicide
key_evidence_accepted: None accepted as establishing abetment; the court found the complainant's and colleagues' statements did not suggest any instigation
witness_credibility: Not assessed on credibility; the court found the prosecution had failed to collect evidence substantiating the allegations
trial_duration: offence: 17.02.2020; trial judgment: 24.02.2022 (trial court order rejecting discharge); High Court: 05.09.2023; Supreme Court: 10 July 2024
legal_representation: Accused: Anand Dilip Landge, Paras Yadav, Sangeeta S. Pahune Patil (Advs.). Respondents (State and complainant): Shrirang B. Varma, Siddharth Dharmadhikari and others (Advs.)
investigation_status: FIR No. 74/2020 registered; charge-sheet filed 04.11.2020 under s.306 IPC; Sessions Case No. 100 of 2021 pending
appeal_history: Trial court: rejected discharge application (24.02.2022). High Court: revision dismissed (05.09.2023). Supreme Court: appeal allowed and discharge granted
prosecution_argument: The ingredients of s.306 IPC were made out from the investigation evidence, so the High Court rightly dismissed the petition
defence_argument: No evidence of an active role; house was jointly purchased so no transfer demand; no grievance raised with authorities before the suicide; allegations fake and frivolous; deceased may have died out of frustration over liquor habit
legal_principle_applied: Abetment under s.306 read with s.107 IPC requires instigation, conspiracy or intentional aid; a positive, proximate act and clear mens rea are needed; the prima facie test was applied to decide discharge
precedent_relied_upon: S.S. Chheena v. Vijay Kumar Mahajan [2010] 9 SCR 1111 : (2010) 12 SCC 190; Amalendu Pal v. State of W.B. [2009] 15 SCR 836 : (2010) 1 SCC 707; Ramesh Kumar v. State of Chhattisgarh [2001] Supp. 4 SCR 247 : (2001) 9 SCC 618 (Gurucharan Singh v. State of Punjab [2020] 8 SCR 741 : (2020) 10 SCC 200 referred to)
other_sentence_order: High Court order set aside; accused discharged from the s.306 IPC proceedings
